codeReview.summary: Solid implementation of evaluator issue gating in the execution loop. The feature correctly wires structured issues (blocking and non-blocking) from the evaluator verdict into the pipeline control flow. Blocking issues halt the pipeline and surface through an optional `requestIssueApproval` method on the ApprovalHandler interface. Non-blocking issues accumulate in StageContext via `_pendingNonBlockingIssues`. The evaluator transport failure graceful degradation path is well-implemented — when `transportError` is true, both the revision loop and issue gating are cleanly skipped. The stage context accumulation block was correctly refactored from a `cachedHandoff`-guarded conditional to an unconditional block, using optional chaining for null safety, ensuring non-blocking issues are accumulated even when handoff is unavailable. EvaluatorInput was extended with `stage_context` so the evaluator for phase N receives cumulative context from prior phases. 18 comprehensive tests cover all expected behaviors including the edge case of mixed blocking/non-blocking issues, pass/fail independence, and backward compatibility with undefined issues arrays.

issues.description: The `else` block for `!transportError` wraps ~200 lines (revision loop + issue gating). While functionally correct, this creates deep nesting and the closing brace at line 852 (`} // end else (not transportError)`) followed immediately by `} // end evaluator guard` can be hard to follow. An early-return or early-continue pattern (e.g., skipping to phase chaining on transportError) would improve readability. Not a bug, but a maintainability concern.

When there are only non-blocking issues and no blocking issues, `_pendingNonBlockingIssues` is assigned but the log message says 'accumulated' which is slightly misleading — they are staged at this point and only truly accumulated into StageContext later (~line 886). Minor naming/logging clarity issue.

The `requestIssueApproval` method delegates to `requestApproval(phaseIndex, description)` where `description` is a multi-line string including issue details. The existing `requestApproval` method emits an `approvalRequested` event with `Phase ${phaseIndex + 1}: ${title}` as the description. When called from `requestIssueApproval`, the `title` parameter already contains the phase prefix and issue details, so the event will contain a redundant `Phase N:` prefix wrapping the already-formatted description. This won't cause a bug but the approval UI may show slightly malformed text like 'Phase 1: Phase 1: Some title\n\nBlocking issues found:...'.

summary: The issue-gating-execution-loop feature is well-implemented. It correctly wires evaluator structured issues into the execution loop with deterministic gating: blocking issues halt the pipeline and surface via the approval gate, non-blocking issues accumulate in stage context, and the behavior is additive to existing pass/fail evaluation. Transport failure graceful degradation is cleanly handled. All 8 expected behaviors from the feature spec are covered by 18 tests. Three non-blocking issues identified: deep nesting from the transportError else block, a slightly misleading log message about issue accumulation timing, and potential double-prefixing in the UIApprovalHandler's issue approval delegation. None are blocking — the implementation is correct and complete.
